newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Timah awaits government word on Busang.
newsitem.headline: Timah awaits government word on Busang.

text.p: Indonesian tin miner PT Tambang Timah said on Monday it was still waiting for a government decision on its participation in the Busang gold project.
"As far as we know, there should be a MOU signing today of all parties involved with Busang," Timah corporate secretary Prasetyo B. Saksono told Reuters.
The company had yet to receive word from the government.
"But what I have heard from the local market was that the MOU has been signed and the companies involved are different from the previous ones," he said.
The company had not heard from the government on whether or not Timah was involved in the project, he said.

Industry sources said on Monday that Canadian mining firm Bre-X Minerals Ltd, Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold of the United States and Indonesian interests signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) for the development of Busang on Sunday.
They said Bre-X would get a 45 percent stake in Busang, Indonesian interests 40 percent and Freeport 15 percent through a new joint-venture company.
"So we are just waiting for an official announcement," Prasetyo said.
Tambang Timah was 150 rupiah lower at 5,125 rupiah, with 6.6 million shares changing hands by midday on Monday. Brokers said it was due to profit taking after significant gains recently.
Some brokers said there was market speculation that Timah might not be involved in the Busang project.
"The market is still speculating on the local parties who will hold the 40 percent stake in the project," a broker with leading European bank said.
